questions.q: Choose the article: *___ agua está fría.*
questions.explain: Agua is feminine but takes el because it starts with a stressed a-.
Problema is one of the Greek-origin -ma nouns, which are masculine.
Most adjectives ending in -or add -a for the feminine.

questions.q: *¿Quieres la camisa azul o *___*?* (the red one)
questions.explain: An article plus adjective can stand for a noun already mentioned, keeping its gender.

questions.q: *Mañana no *___* salir.* (we won't be able to)
questions.explain: Poder has the irregular future stem podr-.

questions.q: *¿Dónde *___* Ana? No contesta.* (I wonder where she is)
questions.explain: The simple future can express a guess about the present.
Decir has the irregular conditional stem dir-.
Before a noun use tanto, agreeing with it: tantos libros.
Before a number, than is de in Spanish.
Bueno has the irregular comparative and superlative mejor, placed before the noun.
A repeated past habit takes the imperfect, and ir is irregular: íbamos.

questions.q: Which is the correct preterite *yo* form of *buscar*?
questions.explain: Verbs in -car change c to qu before -é.

questions.q: *Ayer mis padres *___* la noticia en el periódico.*
questions.explain: When the stem ends in a vowel, -ieron becomes -yeron.
Stem-changing -ir verbs change o to u in the third-person preterite.
After a j stem, the third-person plural ending is -eron.
The location of an event uses ser, not estar.
Estar with food describes how it tastes right now.

questions.q: *Tu coche es nuevo, pero *___* es viejo.* (mine)
questions.explain: A possessive pronoun takes an article and agrees with the noun it replaces, here masculine coche.

questions.q: *¿Qué es *___*?* (an unknown object you are holding)
questions.explain: The neutral esto refers to something unidentified near the speaker.
A + el must contract to al.
Thanks are an exchange, so they take por.
Deadlines take para.
The action in progress that gets interrupted takes the imperfect.

questions.q: *Ayer *___* a tu hermano en la fiesta.* (met for the first time)
questions.explain: Conocer in the preterite means to meet someone for the first time.
Con + mí fuses into conmigo.
Negative tú commands use the present subjunctive: no digas.

questions.q: *Le di el libro a Ana.* → *___ di.*
questions.explain: Le becomes se before lo, and the indirect pronoun comes first.
Encantar agrees with the thing loved, and an infinitive counts as singular; les refers to the parents.
Machines and devices use funcionar, not trabajar.

questions.q: *___ tres años que vivo en Lima.*
questions.explain: Hace + time + que + present says how long something has been going on; hace is always singular.
